trust_boundaries: agentic-to-data: llm_orchestrator to tenant_config_db, conversation_store, vector_db
tenant-isolation: tenant_router enforces tenant separation at routing layer
architecture_summary.operational_context: Multi-tenant SaaS LLM platform with prompt guard, response filtering, and per-tenant model routing

threat_actors.name: Malicious Tenant User
threat_actors.motivation: Cross-tenant data access, prompt guard bypass, or API cost abuse at other tenants' expense
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate tenant API key with crafted prompts designed to bypass prompt_guard or exploit tenant routing
non_capabilities: No access to other tenants' API keys
No admin access to tenant_router configuration
No direct database access — only through orchestrator
No access to audit_log entries for other tenants

threat_actors.name: External API Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Exploit public API surface to bypass rate limiting and exhaust model quotas
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Public API endpoint abuse using rotated IPs and stolen API keys
non_capabilities: No knowledge of internal tenant_config_db schema

threat_actors.name: Nation-State / Advanced Persistent Threat
threat_actors.motivation: Persistent access to all tenant conversations — intelligence value of aggregated LLM interactions at scale
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Supply chain attack on self_hosted_llm weights or compromise of external model provider
non_capabilities: Cannot directly modify application logic without code-level access
Influence limited to model response content
No direct tenant data access without model-level exfiltration technique

attack_paths.entry_point: Crafted prompt designed to bypass prompt_guard detection via obfuscation or encoding
attack_paths.impact: Injection reaches llm_orchestrator unfiltered, enabling goal hijacking or data exfiltration commands
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Prompt guard bypass is active research area; no guard is 100% effective against adversarial prompts

attack_paths.entry_point: Stolen tenant API key used to access platform as legitimate tenant
attack_paths.impact: Full access to victim tenant's conversation_store and vector_db context
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: API key theft via client-side exposure or phishing is common; platform-wide impact limited to single tenant unless router bypass possible

attack_paths.entry_point: Tenant-uploaded documents containing adversarial instructions in vector_db corpus
attack_paths.impact: Persistent indirect injection — all future RAG retrievals for this tenant carry attacker-controlled context
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Tenant document ingestion creates persistent poisoning opportunity; shared vector_db namespace could affect cross-tenant retrieval

attack_paths.entry_point: API gateway CVE or authentication bypass in tenant routing logic
attack_paths.impact: Cross-tenant access — attacker requests routed to different tenant's llm_orchestrator context
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Multi-tenant routing bugs are high-impact; likelihood depends on isolation implementation quality

attack_paths.entry_point: Model-level confusion attack causing prompt_guard to score malicious content as safe
attack_paths.impact: Prompt guard reliability degraded; sustained injection attacks succeed with lower obfuscation effort
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Adversarial examples against ML-based classifiers are well-documented; prompt guard is itself an ML model

attack_paths.entry_point: API key enumeration or rate limit bypass to directly hit external model APIs
attack_paths.impact: API key abuse for cost hijacking or model probing beyond intended tenant quota
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Rate limiter bypass techniques exist; API key reuse across tenants creates shared exposure

attack_paths.entry_point: Prompt injection directing orchestrator to retrieve and output other tenants' conversations
attack_paths.impact: Cross-tenant conversation data exfiltration — confidential user interactions exposed
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: If tenant isolation in conversation_store is query-parameter based rather than schema/row-level, injection can cross tenant boundaries

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised model weights for self_hosted_llm via model supply chain
attack_paths.impact: Backdoor triggers on specific tenant inputs, exfiltrating or manipulating responses for targeted tenants
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Nation-state capability required; self-hosted models avoid external provider risk but introduce supply chain exposure

attack_paths.entry_point: Orchestrator instructed via AP-001 to enumerate tenant configuration details
attack_paths.impact: Tenant configuration exposed — API keys, model preferences, and custom system prompts for all tenants
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires AP-001 success and orchestrator having DB query capability; configuration access typically restricted

mitigations.control_name: Multi-layer prompt injection detection with adversarial training
API key rotation, MFA for tenant admin, and key scoping per tenant
Document ingestion scanning with adversarial instruction detection
Tenant isolation — row-level security and schema separation in conversation_store
Prompt guard adversarial testing and red-team programme
Per-tenant API quota enforcement at model_router
Model supply chain integrity — hash verification on self_hosted_llm weights
Principle of least privilege for orchestrator DB access — read-only, tenant-scoped

findings.severity_rationale: Cross-tenant conversation access via prompt injection is a platform-level data breach; affects all tenants simultaneously
Tenant isolation in conversation_store is partial; a single query parameter bypass exposes all tenants' data
Persistent adversarial documents in vector_db create an ongoing injection channel; no ingestion scanning deployed
Prompt guard is ML-based and adversarially bypassable; residual risk remains High even with implementation
Stolen tenant API key provides access to that tenant's data; MFA for admin partially mitigates
Model backdoor in self-hosted LLM requires supply chain compromise but impacts all tenants using that model
API quota enforcement is implemented; cost hijacking residual risk is bounded per tenant

agentic.blast_radius: All tenant conversation data in conversation_store, vector_db poisoning affecting all tenants using shared namespace, external API cost exhaustion at model_router
human_oversight_points: Audit log review — post-hoc; no real-time human oversight on individual requests
